content_units: Formula: Return rate \(= \frac{\text{returns}}{\text{sales}} \times 100\), ROAS \(= \frac{\text{sales}}{\text{ad spend}}\), Conversion proxy \(= \frac{\text{sales}}{\text{website visits}}\)
Month   Sales   Returns   Ad Spend   Website Visits   Return Rate   ROAS   Sales per Visit
Option 1: Monthly sales trend line   Best top-level chart for overall business momentum   Shows growth and soft dips clearly
Option 2: Combo chart for sales and ad spend   Use bars for sales and a line for ad spend   Best for checking whether spend is scaling with revenue
Option 3: Returns rate line chart   Plot monthly return rate %   Highlights quality or fulfillment issues faster than raw returns
Option 4: Website visits vs sales dual-axis chart   Compare traffic and revenue together   Useful for spotting demand vs conversion efficiency shifts
Option 5: ROAS bar chart   Monthly return on ad spend by month   Strong for marketing efficiency decisions
Option 6: KPI cards   Sales, return rate, ROAS, and visits totals/averages   Best summary layer above charts
-   Sales trend is positive overall.   Sales rose from 42,000 in January to a peak of 53,000 in May, then eased slightly to 51,700 in June.
-   February was the weakest month.   It had the lowest sales, lower traffic, and the highest return rate at 6.0%, making it the clearest underperformance point.
-   Traffic growth supported revenue growth.   Website visits climbed from 18,000 in January to 22,900 in May, closely matching the upward sales trend.
-   Marketing efficiency stayed very stable.   ROAS remained tightly clustered around 12x every month, suggesting ad spend scaled efficiently without major waste.
-   March and June stand out for quality/efficiency.   March had the lowest return rate at 4.2%, while June delivered the best sales-per-visit value at 2.34 despite slightly lower traffic than May.
